Appearance:
 Shri Rukvendra Singh Ghuraiya - Advocate for the applic
 Shri Harish Sharma -Dy.
Advocate General for the State.
Shri Rohit Tiwari - Advocate for the complainant.

Order 
This is the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of B.N.S.S/S.439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail.

He has been arrested on 28.09.2024 in connection with Crime No.107 of 2024 registered at Police Station Chinnor, District Gwalior for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 465, 467, 468 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code.

The only allegation against the present applicant is that he was a witness to the registry of the property, which was alleged to be forged and was got executed by impersonation by co-accused to be the actual owner and on the basis of his signatures on the sale deed and thereafter, he had role to play in obtaining loan from the Bank.
On the basis of such allegation, the present F.I.R. has been registered against the applicant.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case, as due to acquaintance with the main accuser persons, he had appended.

It is further submitted that there is no part of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:19647 2 MCRC-46216-2024 the applicant in the commission of alleged offence, as no recovery has been intended from him.
It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of District Gwalior and there is no likelihood of his absconsion or tampering with the prosecution evidence.

sentences.text: The applicant is aged about 30 years and confinement may bring him social disrepute and personal inconvenience.
Applicant undertakes to cooperate in investigation/trial and would not be a source of embarrassment and harassment in any manner to the complainant party side.
The applicant is ready and willing to abide by any condition which may be imposed by this Court in case of grant of bail.
On the basis of the above submissions, the present applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
Per contra , learned counsel for the respondent/State as well as counsel for the complainant had vehemently opposed the present bail application and had prayed for its rejection.

After considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case as well as contentions of the parties and the fact that the trial is not likely to conclude in near future and prolonged pretrial detention being an anathema to the concept of liberty, this Court is inclined to extend the benefit of bail to the applicant.

Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed and it is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lac only) with two solvent sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court/committal Court for his appearance on the dates given by the concerned Court.

This order will remain operative subject to compliance of the following conditions by the applicant :-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:19647 3 MCRC-46216-2024 1.
The applicant will not move in the vicinity of complainant party and applicant will not seek unnecessary adjournments during the trial; and 6.
The applicant will not leave India without previous permission of the trial Court/Investigating Officer, as the case may be.
Application stands disposed of in above terms.
Let a copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance.
